question:
RECOMMEND: APPROVE — advance to build.

Why: every ruling you gave is folded in, the riskiest mechanisms were exercised rather than assumed, and three separate times on this feature refusing to inherit a claim caught a real error. Nothing in this spec now rests on an unread fact. Build has real work it can start, and it cannot touch your live data without you.

DECISION EFFECT: approve advances 061 to build in a dedicated worktree and dispatches a build agent to write the extractor, the importer and their tests. Nothing is written to your data by this approval — the import cannot run until you approve the normalization sheet (AC-14), and the staging rehearsal precedes any production write. Reject holds 061 at spec with your feedback.

ONE DECISION LEFT, AND IT IS SMALL: how to make staging "the same".

Your ruling was "use prod categories, make sure the sage tis the same." Part one is settled: production is the authority, and nothing is ever written to production's Categories tab. Part two admits a destructive reading, so it is yours:

- R1 (RECOMMENDED, AND THE DEFAULT IF YOU SAY NOTHING). Add the three missing production categories to staging under new ids — cat_026 Tenant, cat_027 Insurance, cat_028 Tax — and LEAVE the existing test entries alone. Staging then resolves every production category name, which is all the rehearsal actually needs. Nothing is deleted.
- R2. Overwrite staging's cat_023 to cat_025 so it is byte-identical to production. Satisfies "the same" literally, and DESTROYS three categories someone may be using — including any staging expense already filed against them, which would silently change meaning rather than break loudly.

Approving without saying anything gets you R1. Choose R2 only if you can confirm Test Cat, Antkee and ScrollTest are yours and disposable.

ONE THING TO KNOW BEFORE APPROVING — not a decision, a loss:

2024-12-17 through 2024-12-31 have no columns in your workbook. The last fifteen days of December 2024 were never entered, so no import can recover them. 2024's imported annual total will be short by whatever you spent that fortnight, and the app will show nothing for those dates. The same applies far more narrowly to 2024-06-16, 2023-06-16, 2023-07-01 and 2023-07-03. If you expected the imported 2024 total to match your own records, this is why it will not.

artifacts.summary:
CHOSEN APPROACH: two scripts, not one. An extractor reads the archive workbook and writes a normalization sheet you review; an importer reads ONLY the approved sheet and writes to the app. Separate deliberately, so your approval sits structurally between them and AC-14 cannot be bypassed with a flag.

YOUR RULINGS, FOLDED:
- 2022 OUT OF SCOPE. Enforced by AC-4, and the guard was exercised rather than proposed: columns A-C are byte-identical across all three year bands, so taxonomy cannot discriminate them. The extractor discovers bands from header rows instead of hard-coded row numbers. Reversing it later is a --years flag.
- STAGING GOES FIRST. Specced with its cost stated: load-local-env.js cannot aim any admin script at staging today, so that plumbing is required work here. The rehearsal — snapshot, apply, verify, hand-add a row, undo, diff — precedes any production write. Credential wrinkle handled: only the staging service account can read your archive workbook; production gets 403.
- D4 = A, recorded as your decision. It costs you nothing; see below.
- D6 part 1: production is the authority for category identity; nothing is ever written to production's Categories tab. Part 2 is the one open item, in the question above.

D4 — YOUR QUESTION, ANSWERED BY PROBE, AND IT DISSOLVED THE DECISION. You asked "is there any expense records?" instead of deciding blind. It had never been asked of the data. Per column:
- Day columns holding data but carrying no parseable date: 0, in both years.
- The 15 duplicated December 2024 dates occupy 30 columns. ALL 30 ARE EMPTY.
- The 16 missing 2024 days and 3 missing 2023 days have no column at all, so can hold nothing by construction.
- Rows with an untrustworthy date: 0 of 774 for 2024, 0 of 893 for 2023. 0.00% of either year sits behind a date we would have to invent.
Option A therefore costs you nothing — no manual pass, because there is nothing to correct. Every one of the ~1,667 imported rows carries a real, unique date from its own column header. Option B, assigning a date a cell did not carry, is not implemented at all, so that failure cannot occur by drift or by a later flag.

WHAT THE D4 AUDIT ALSO FOUND — A DEFECT IN THIS SPEC'S OWN PARSER. Chasing the arithmetic exposed that AC-3's discriminator, keying on the 金額 column label, SILENTLY DROPPED THREE REAL EXPENSE RECORDS in column MI. AC-3 is recut, and AC-19 is new: a whole-band accounting assertion that unaccounted cells are 0 in both years. AC-19 is the only criterion in the set that checks we did not MISS something, rather than that what we took is correct. Every other criterion verifies the rows we imported; this one verifies we imported all of them.

A SECOND SILENT-DROP TRAP, MEASURED: 10 cells in 2024 and 47 in 2023 store amounts as text rather than numbers. They are plain digit strings, so they parse — but a parser accepting only real numbers would silently drop 47 real 2023 amounts rather than fail loudly. Any value that genuinely fails to parse now aborts the run naming the source cell; it never quietly becomes zero.

THE RECUT CRITERIA rest on references we control, so your workbook's own ~12% internal disagreement can no longer fail a check meant to catch OUR bugs:
- AC-2 joins the app to the approved normalization sheet on a key and compares per-year sums EXACTLY in integer minor units, not within 1%. A tolerance could only hide our own arithmetic error.
- AC-3 recut after the MI finding above.
- AC-4 asserts no row dated outside 2023-2024 reached the app, and that the extractor discovers bands rather than taking row numbers.
- The old AC-2's subject survives as AC-15: the variance report must exist and cover all 24 in-scope year-months, while the exit code stays INDEPENDENT of its contents. Its falsifier is making the run fail on a variance threshold — reintroducing the old AC-2.

THE MECHANISM THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED SILENTLY: category ids are not portable between environments. Read live rather than trusted from source constants, staging and production Categories tabs both use cat_NNN and disagree from cat_023 onward. A mapping built and rehearsed on staging would have filed production rows under wrong categories while every id-exists check still passed. AC-9 resolves each name against the target's own tab at run time and aborts before writing if any fails; D3 gains a production pre-flight no staging rehearsal can substitute for.

DO YOUR HAND CORRECTIONS SURVIVE A RE-GENERATE? Yes, and the mechanism is never-overwrite rather than merge-in-place. Generate aborts on an existing tab; re-generation writes a new version and carries corrections forward by source coordinate rather than row position; an irreconcilable conflict exits non-zero listing the keys; a vanished source cell becomes orphaned rather than disappearing. If the carry-forward is itself buggy the previous version still exists untouched, so recovery is re-running the carry, not re-doing your work. AC-16 covers it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: 20, each with Verified by and Falsified by. Mostly offline; AC-7 and AC-8 interactive, judged on a live drive with no harness built to automate them. AC-20 covers the staging categories write, which must be reversible. The ac-scan was exercised, not asserted — an earlier run read only 15 of 16 because italics nested inside a bold heading broke the parse; fixed, and it now lists every criterion and exits 0.

FIDELITY LIMIT: 2024-12-17 through 2024-12-31 have no columns in the source. The app will show no spending for the last fifteen days of December 2024, and 2024's imported annual total is short by whatever was spent then. No import can recover data that was never entered.

CHECKLIST ACCOUNTING: 10 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed.
